nodes.description: Biallelic POC1B variants. Missense and in-frame alleles such as p.Arg106Pro and p.Gln67del lost basal-body localization in overexpressed RPE1 cells and lost the interaction with FAM161A, although p.Arg106Pro localized normally to the centrosome in a separate HEK293T assay, so the localization defect is assay-dependent; nonsense, frameshift and splice alleles, including a deep-intronic variant that activates a pseudoexon, are predicted to remove the protein.

evidence.reference_title: An interaction network of inner centriole proteins organised by POC1A-POC1B heterodimer crosslinks ensures centriolar integrity.
evidence.snippet: We demonstrate the importance of an interaction network organised by POC1A-POC1B heterodimers within the centriole lumen, where the WD40 domain of POC1B localises close to the centriole wall, while the POC5-interacting WD40 of POC1A resides in the centriole lumen.

evidence.reference_title: An interaction network of inner centriole proteins organised by POC1A-POC1B heterodimer crosslinks ensures centriolar integrity.
evidence.snippet: Disruption of POC1A or POC1B leads to centriole microtubule defects and deletion of both genes causes centriole disintegration.

evidence.reference_title: Disruption of the basal body protein POC1B results in autosomal-recessive cone-rod dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: Upon overexpression of POC1B in human TERT-immortalized retinal pigment epithelium 1 cells, the encoded wild-type protein localized to the basal body of the primary cilium, whereas this localization was lost for p.Arg106Pro and p.Gln67del variant forms of POC1B.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation of POC1B in a severe syndromic retinal ciliopathy.
evidence.snippet: In HEK293T cells transfected with a plasmid containing the p.Arg106Pro mutation, the protein localized normally at the centrosome

evidence.reference_title: Clinical Characteristics of POC1B-Associated Retinopathy and Assignment of Pathogenicity to Novel Deep Intronic and Non-Canonical Splice Site Variants.
evidence.snippet: Splicing analysis revealed that the non-canonical splice site variant c.561-3T>C leads to exon skipping while the novel deep intronic variant c.1033-327T>A causes pseudoexon activation.

evidence.reference_title: A novel homozygous missense variant in POC1B causes cone dystrophy in a consanguineous Pakistani family.
evidence.snippet: Full visual field tests showed bilateral central scotoma, while single visual field tests indicated bilateral generalized depression of the visual field.

evidence.snippet: relative central scotoma, mild peripheral constriction (13 years)

nodes.description: Cone dystrophy or cone-rod dystrophy, usually with onset in childhood to early adulthood and a slowly progressive course. Night blindness was not reported in the original consanguineous family.

evidence.reference_title: Novel recessive cone-rod dystrophy caused by POC1B mutation.
evidence.snippet: POC1B is a novel gene for a new disease typical of CORD except that patients did not report night blindness. The clinical course was slowly progressive.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical Characteristics of POC1B-Associated Retinopathy and Assignment of Pathogenicity to Novel Deep Intronic and Non-Canonical Splice Site Variants.
evidence.snippet: All patients displayed a similar, slowly progressive retinopathy (cone dystrophy or cone-rod dystrophy) with normal funduscopy but disrupted outer retinal layers on optical coherence tomography and variable age of onset.

evidence.reference_title: Novel recessive cone-rod dystrophy caused by POC1B mutation.
evidence.snippet: The clinical phenotype was typical CORD with photophobia, decreased central vision, and dyschromatopsia.

evidence.reference_title: A novel homozygous missense variant in POC1B causes cone dystrophy in a consanguineous Pakistani family.
evidence.snippet: The proband, a 63-years old male, showed severely reduced day vision, a visual acuity of counting fingers (CF), color vision deficiency, high myopia and photophobia.

nodes.description: No disease-modifying treatment exists. Management is supportive: low-vision aids, tinted or filtered lenses for photophobia, and periodic ophthalmological follow-up. Genetic testing is what separates the disorder from incomplete achromatopsia, which it resembles.

Oligoasthenoteratozoospermia with male infertility, reported together with cone-rod dystrophy in two brothers homozygous for a POC1B frameshift variant. Whether it accompanies other POC1B genotypes is not known.

evidence.reference_title: Homozygous frameshift variant in POC1B causes male infertility with oligoasthenoteratozoospermia in human and mice.
evidence.snippet: Here, whole-exome sequencing was performed to identify a homozygous frameshift variant (c.151delG) in POC1B in the two brothers who had been diagnosed with both CORD and OAT from a consanguineous family.

nodes.description: Nystagmus, sometimes present from early infancy together with poor visual acuity, giving an achromatopsia-like presentation; it was present in two of the four patients in the gene-discovery report.

evidence.reference_title: Disruption of the basal body protein POC1B results in autosomal-recessive cone-rod dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: in another sibling and in one isolated individual, poor visual acuity and nystagmus were present from early infancy, suggesting a form of ACHM.

evidence.reference_title: Disruption of the basal body protein POC1B results in autosomal-recessive cone-rod dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: The proband (A-II:1) of family A presented with reduced visual acuity in early infancy and mild nystagmus.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical Characteristics of POC1B-Associated Retinopathy and Assignment of Pathogenicity to Novel Deep Intronic and Non-Canonical Splice Site Variants.
evidence.snippet: All patients showed impaired cone function leading to reduced visual acuity, color vision disturbances, photophobia or nystagmus.

evidence.reference_title: Severe Joubert syndrome in family with homozygous POC1B p.Arg106Pro variant is due to a co-inherited deep-intronic mutation in the neighboring CEP290 gene.
evidence.snippet: EOSRD and PKD can fully be ascribed to this CEP290 variant, whose effect outshines the "background" non-syndromic POC1B retinopathy and co-segregates with the severe syndromic phenotype. Our novel findings in this family no longer justify POC1B as a JBTS gene.

evidence.reference_title: Novel recessive cone-rod dystrophy caused by POC1B mutation.
evidence.snippet: The clinical phenotype was typical CORD with photophobia, decreased central vision, and dyschromatopsia.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical Characteristics of POC1B-Associated Retinopathy and Assignment of Pathogenicity to Novel Deep Intronic and Non-Canonical Splice Site Variants.
evidence.snippet: Other symptoms were decreased visual acuity and photophobia.

nodes.description: POC1B is a centriolar WD40-repeat protein that, together with POC1A, maintains centriole integrity. In photoreceptors it localizes to the basal body and centriole adjacent to the connecting cilium, the specialized primary cilium through which outer-segment proteins are transported. Loss of POC1B function disrupts this sensory cilium; in zebrafish knockdown the connecting cilia are shortened and reduced and the outer segments are shortened.

evidence.reference_title: Mutation of POC1B in a severe syndromic retinal ciliopathy.
evidence.snippet: In human and mouse retina, POC1B localized to the basal body and centriole adjacent to the connecting cilium of photoreceptors and in synapses of the outer plexiform layer.

evidence.reference_title: Poc1A and Poc1B act together in human cells to ensure centriole integrity.
evidence.snippet: Hence, Poc1A and Poc1B play redundant, but essential, roles in generation of stable centrioles, but Poc1B may have additional independent functions during cell cycle progression.

evidence.reference_title: Knockdown of poc1b causes abnormal photoreceptor sensory cilium and vision impairment in zebrafish.
evidence.snippet: These data suggest that poc1b is required for normal development and ciliogenesis of retinal photoreceptor sensory cilia and other cilia.

nodes.description: Optical coherence tomography shows absence of the interdigitation zone (cone outer segment tip line) and a blurred ellipsoid zone, often with a normal fundus on ophthalmoscopy.

evidence.reference_title: Phenotypical Characteristics of POC1B-Associated Retinopathy in Japanese Cohort: Cone Dystrophy With Normal Funduscopic Appearance.
evidence.snippet: Optical coherence tomography revealed an absence of the interdigitation zone and blurred ellipsoid zone in the posterior pole, but the foveal structures were preserved in three cases.

evidence.reference_title: Novel recessive cone-rod dystrophy caused by POC1B mutation.
evidence.snippet: In all patients, a disrupted inner segment/outer segment line and the external limiting membrane were noted as a single blurry line at the central fovea, and the cone outer segment tip line was absent.

nodes.description: CRISPR knock-in of the frameshift allele found in two brothers with cone-rod dystrophy and oligoasthenoteratozoospermia.

Photoreceptor degeneration affecting cones first and most. Most patients have generalized or peripheral cone dystrophy with normal dark-adapted responses; rod responses become subnormal in some patients and a minority progress to frank cone-rod dystrophy. Structurally the outer retina shows loss of the interdigitation zone (cone outer segment tips) and a blurred ellipsoid zone, often with a normal-appearing fundus. Severity ranges from early-childhood onset to a late-onset mild form with relatively preserved cone function.

evidence.reference_title: Phenotypical Characteristics of POC1B-Associated Retinopathy in Japanese Cohort: Cone Dystrophy With Normal Funduscopic Appearance.
evidence.snippet: Generalized or peripheral cone dystrophy with normal funduscopic appearance is the representative phenotype of POC1B-associated retinopathy in our cohort.

evidence.reference_title: A homozygous POC1B variant causes recessive cone-rod dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: Follow-up three years later showed progression to a cone-rod dystrophy.

evidence.reference_title: A mild form of POC1B-associated retinal dystrophy with relatively preserved cone system function.
evidence.snippet: We reported the case of an older patient with POC1B-associated retinopathy, demonstrating late-onset visual decrease, good visual acuity, and relatively preserved cone system function.

nodes.description: Decreased central vision, the usual presenting complaint.

evidence.reference_title: Case of cone dystrophy with normal fundus appearance associated with biallelic POC1B variants.
evidence.snippet: The patient was a 20-year-old Japanese man whose chief complaint was a progressive decrease in his central vision.

evidence.reference_title: Phenotypic and genotypic features of POC1B-associated cone dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: Ophthalmic examination showed decreased Snellen visual acuities (range: 20/100-20/300) and color vision bilaterally.

nodes.description: In the one family reported with both cone-rod dystrophy and oligoasthenoteratozoospermia, POC1B protein was absent from sperm, and mice knocked in for the same frameshift allele showed abnormal acrosome and flagellum formation.

evidence.snippet: Additionally, testicular histology and transmission electron microscopy analysis of the testes and sperm indicated that Poc1b mutation results in abnormal formation of acrosomes and flagella.

nodes.description: Full-field photopic responses are reduced to non-recordable while scotopic responses are normal or subnormal, the electrophysiological signature of a cone-predominant dystrophy.

evidence.reference_title: Novel recessive cone-rod dystrophy caused by POC1B mutation.
evidence.snippet: Cone response was nonrecordable in all patients, whereas rod response was nonrecordable in the eldest patient and subnormal in the others.

evidence.reference_title: Phenotypic and genotypic features of POC1B-associated cone dystrophy.
evidence.snippet: Full-field electroretinography demonstrated undetectable light-adapted responses and normal dark-adapted responses in all patients.

evidence.reference_title: Phenotypical Characteristics of POC1B-Associated Retinopathy in Japanese Cohort: Cone Dystrophy With Normal Funduscopic Appearance.
evidence.snippet: The full-field photopic ERGs were reduced or extinguished with normal scotopic responses.
